cases.question: What is a linked list?
cases.reference_answer: A linked list stores nodes connected by next pointers.

cases.question: What does the head pointer identify?
cases.reference_answer: The head pointer identifies the first node.

cases.question: What is the head of an empty linked list?
cases.reference_answer: An empty list has a null head.

cases.question: Explain insertion at the beginning of a linked list.
cases.reference_answer: Connect the new node to the previous head, then update the head pointer to the new node.

cases.question: How does insertion preserve the existing chain?
cases.reference_answer: Connect the new node to the previous head before changing head.

cases.question: What happens if the new node next pointer is set to NULL before updating head?
cases.reference_answer: The old nodes become unreachable.

cases.question: Why can the first insertion pass while insertion into a non-empty list fails?
cases.reference_answer: A NULL next pointer loses old nodes when head is replaced.

cases.question: How do we count the nodes?
cases.reference_answer: Start at head, increment count for each visited node and follow next until NULL.

cases.question: How many nodes does an empty list have?
cases.reference_answer: An empty list has zero nodes.

cases.question: Explain linked-list insertion and how to count nodes afterward.
cases.reference_answer: Connect new node to previous head, update head, then traverse next and count each visited node.

cases.question: Explain the diagram on page 2.
